5) ubAdd(label,fn) and userBias(a,ctx,why): additive, clamped to 1.2, the ONLY way user-derived influence enters localChoose. Add a ubVeto stub. Move round-1 user nudges into terms.
6) bondOf/tierOf shim over friendW, know and chats, with TIERS [0,10,60,160,320,600].
7) HOME_CAPS, hasItem, capSpot, and FEAT={nest:false} (radio false until B21).
8) The deterministic Seattle WX almanac (forDate, at, WIND) drives WEATHER.kind. catchUp and the diary read WX.at. Keep the rollWeather overrides.
9) isPresent().
10) EV emitters DOOREV and SFXEV, sfx(), and no-op emote()/setFace() stubs.
11) Fix savePhotos: the keep-set is posts(24) ∪ S.you.album ∪ S.wend.pol ∪ S.pins, with a 3.2e6-char budget and 512 px JPEG at .72.
12) The draws.json ledger, a portrait perf variant and __mocha.drawCalls().
Everything migrate/catchUp reads is declared above them and hoisted. No per-frame allocation. Aim for 12 to 15 KB.

steps.title: Street navigation and agent routes
steps.brief:
Full spec: section B10 of /tmp/harness/round2-spec.md.
Replace the 17-node NODES/NADJ with a NAV graph (keep wPath as a wrapper): sidewalk lines at road ±4.6, corners and crosswalks (including mid-block ones at Maple Row x=40 and Main St x=-21.5 and x=40), and EXTRA_PATHS (alley, square ring, promenade, piers, lake loop, cemetery lane, Willa's path, lot fronts). Each door gets a chain: sidewalk node, approach, threshold (DOOR flag), entry. Use Float32Array storage, Dijkstra with preallocated arrays, and an LRU of 64 routes, cleared on lock or lot changes. Edge flags: COVERED (cheaper in rain), SCENIC, and SECRET shortcuts Mocha discovers.
Interior grids: capture furniture AABBs into p.grid at .5 resolution, inflated by .35. Use A* plus string-pulling, and make regrid(p) re-runnable.
Agents follow routes from a per-agent Float32Array(192) with a 1.5 look-ahead. On DOOR edges they request, hold, then pass.

Explore strolls may cut across grass only when the path is clear of footprints. Rewire Wendell's W.path. Expose navRoute for keepers (B22 moves them).
Street manners: a crosswalk pause, a keep-right offset, soft separation, sidestep after 3 s, and a replan when a door is locked. Speed is about 8. catchUp stays teleport-based. Draw calls unchanged.

steps.title: Walker collision, tap-to-go, seats and vertical transport

Vertical transport: a Sky Needle glass elevator capsule (8 s, replaces deckY flying), the lighthouse '98 steps' climb, wheel and ferry boarding via G.ride, and bike lanes at road ±1.8 with bike racks where the parked bike stays visible.

Compute its bounds at load from PLACES, ROADS and PIERS plus a 6-unit margin, at least x[-107,166] and z[-136,136] (the piers reach x=-101 and the arcade spans about x -95 to -85; the old fixed bounds missed them). QUIET COMPANIONSHIP is his choice only: the userBias term seatedNear (+.6 when he is idle within 25 and his tier with you is friend or higher) feeds a weighted candidate, at most once per 10 min. Never force it.

TRACK S, step 4 of 4 (last; after B27Sa, B27Sb and LF3 on the same file).

steps.title: Elegant pop-ups: names, speech, prompts and notices that make sense

OWNER (Nov 3, 9 AM PT, on his iPhone): "When I was at the cafe, it froze. You have to check these menus, and sometimes what's happening gets in the way. I think we can have pop-ups happening, with the names and stuff, but it needs to come in a more elegant way. Sometimes the bubbles and stuff are all over the place, getting... don't make a lot of sense." Build ONE calm, Animal-Crossing-like presentation layer for everything that pops up over the world, replacing today's scattered floating labels, bubbles and toasts. CORE: (1) PLACE NAMES: no more permanent floating labels over every building. Show a small elegant name card (paper style from Addendum S, serif title + one-line subtitle like 'Drizzle & Bean Cafe, open till 7') that fades in at the top centre for ~2.5 s when the walker arrives in front of a place or enters an area, or when Mocha arrives somewhere in follow mode; then fades out. Optional faint world label only for the place directly in front of the walker within ~6 units. The big map keeps all names. (2) SPEECH: one consistent bubble style anchored to the speaker's head with a little tail, max 2 short lines (longer text pages with a tap), never overlapping the HUD or each other: at most ONE world bubble at a time near the camera focus (Mocha first, then whoever is talking to you, then the nearest NPC); other NPC chatter is queued or dropped, never stacked; bubbles from characters off-screen or behind walls are not shown (Mocha off-screen uses the existing edge chip, with his line inside it). (3) PROMPTS: a single context button above the right-thumb area ('Talk to Juniper', 'Enter', 'Sit', 'Shop') that appears only when facing something interactable, with the same paper style; no duplicate pills. (4) NOTICES: one notice lane (top centre under the status pill) with a queue: one at a time, 2.5 s each, merged when similar ('+24 coins' instead of three toasts), rate-limited (catalog milestones etc.), tap to dismiss; never covering the stick, the look area, cards or sheets. (5) QUIET WHILE BUSY: while any card, sheet, menu, talk card, Your Look, decorate or the map is open, world bubbles/names/notices pause and queue (except the speaker you are talking to), and resume calmly after. (6) THE CAFE FREEZE: reproduce what the owner hit at the cafe on a throttled phone (CDP CPU throttle 4x, 393x852): enter, walk to the counter, talk to Juniper, open the item card / see everything / buy, sit at a table, while NPC chatter and Mocha are around; fix every main-thread stall over 100 ms and every tap that does nothing (including elements intercepting taps). STRETCH: subtle sound ticks for name cards and notices; a 'Show place names' setting (Auto / Always / Off).

Here's the plan for round 2. I rebuilt it into 36 smaller steps so each one can be done well, and I reordered it so the things you asked for land early. A few ideas go beyond what you asked.

**Mocha and Wendell hanging out, with lights in the houses**
- Every house now lights up like the shops: room by room, depending on who's home and what they're doing. You'll see a blue glow when Wendell has a movie on, a nightlight when someone's asleep, and windows coming on one by one at the real Seattle sunset.
- The lights also carry little messages between friends:
  - Wendell flicks his porch light twice to say goodnight when Mocha's window comes on, and Mocha may flick his back.
  - Mocha leaves his porch lantern on for you.
  - If he stopped by your cabin while you were away, a small candle glows in your window.
- Wendell gets a real cottage with a fireplace, an old TV that plays the late show, and a never-ending jigsaw puzzle.
- They have 17 things to do together, like checkers by the fire, radio nights and movie nights.
- Hangouts work even in an empty house: a floor picnic, tea on a moving box, flashlight stories ("i'm literally a ghost").
- You can pull up a chair and drop in on a hangout. Wendell might make you the referee, and Mocha passes you the popcorn.

**Doors, layouts and better looks**
- Everyone walks the sidewalks and goes in and out through doors that really open.
- Knocking never makes Mocha jump up. He just calls "it's open!" from wherever he is.
- The inside of every shop gets a sensible layout, and the whole town gets a softer, cozier look.
- The street lamps light up in a wave at sunset.

**You and the townsfolk**
- Your character is a round-headed little neighbor in a forest-green or blue rain jacket (never yellow, anywhere in the game).
- You can wear a plaid flannel tied around your waist, just like in your reference picture.
- You can walk up to anyone and talk. They ask you questions back and remember your answers.
- The townsfolk now live fuller lives:
  - Pals stop and chat on the sidewalk, and visit each other after closing.
  - Each one works on a little weekly project you can watch, like Hank's birdhouse, which a pair of chickadees moves into on Sunday.
- Talking to Mocha never freezes him. He answers over his shoulder and keeps doing what he chose to do.

**Music**
- The town has its own gentle music that changes with the hour and the rain.
- Mocha picks music from his very first day, without buying anything:
  - a hand-me-down radio from his parents with three stations
  - a jukebox in the square
  - a request box at the record shop, where his pick can become the whole town's music for a while
- Over time, the town's own music slowly leans toward his favorite style.
- It plays even when your iPhone is on silent. Little notes float from his window, and a "Listen in" button lets you hear what he's playing from anywhere.

**Your home and shopping**
- You get a log cabin across the street from Mocha, plus five new shops and 150 items sitting on real shelves.
- Decorating is easy on a phone.
- Mocha and Wendell come to visit on their own. Wendell's first visit brings a jar of his sister's jam.

- A guestbook on your porch collects a line from every visitor. There are no scores or ratings.
- A dish of peanuts for the crows may earn you little trinkets in your mailbox.

**Safety and battery**
- Mocha stays fully in charge of his own life. Anything you do only gently informs him, and his choices always come first.
- Claude is used only a little, about 10 times a day by default.
- Your save is backed up before the big upgrade.
- Photos can't get wiped, and the app stays light on your battery.
